To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we demonstrate a new approach to control the magnetic properties of individual nanoparticles by using large biaxially applied mechanical stress.

(1) large magneto-elastic effects are observed in embedded nanoparticles; (2) stress-induced modifications of the effective magnetic anisotropic field are observed; (3) the magnetic anisotropic constant can be modified by stress.
the application of large biaxal stress to nanoparticles embedded into a non-magnetic matrix can significantly modify their magnetic properties.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new concept for tailoring magnetic properties of nanoparticles through application of large biaxal stress.

the development of new magnetic materials with improved magnetic properties, which can be used for the fabrication of future data storage media with increased storage density and improved performance.
the development of a novel concept for the design and fabrication of high density magnetic data-storage devices based on magnetic nanoparticles.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the magnetic anisotropic properties of nanoparticles can be modified by large mechanical stress.
the application of stress to the nanoparticles embedded in a film can be used as a means to modify their magnetic properties.
the magnetic properties can indeed be adjusted by applying stress to the nanoparticles, and that this approach can be used to tailor the magnetic properties of magnetic nanoparticles.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we can control the magnetic properties of the nanoparticles by applying mechanical stress.
we were able to show that by applying a large mechanical stress on embedded Fe nanoparticles we can modify their magnetic properties.
the magnetic anisotropic energy of the nanoparticles is significantly modified by large mechanical stress.
The main takeaway from our work is that
stress induced magnetic effects are a powerful and simple tool to tune the magnetic properties of magnetic nanoparticles, in particular the anisotropy.
by applying large mechanical stress to magnetic nanoparticles embedded in a thin film, the effective magnetic anisotrpy is significantly modified.
by applying a large mechanical stress to nanoparticles embedded into a non-magnetic substrate, it is possible to modify significantly the magnetic properties of the nanoparticles.
